# PEN-5982 — 30 s per-test timeout for the vendored suite

Tracking: [PEN-5982](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-5982)

Test-config only. `vitest.config.ts` now sets `test.testTimeout: 30_000`, and
`src/vitest-config.test.ts` fails if it drops below 30 s. No vendored source
under `src/` changed other than that new guard test.

## Why

This suite runs its slowest tests at 60-66% of vitest's 5 s default, so the
margin between routine and fatal is ~1.7 s. Measured on CI job `128429016429`
(`merge_group` batch `bb8e52ca`, run `42381210491`, 2026-11-07T14:21Z):

| ms | file | % of 5000 ms |
|---|---|---|
| 3317 | `execute.test.ts` — waits through transient PVC binding | 66 % |
| 3301 | `execute.test.ts` — no scheduler timeout once pod assigned | 66 % |
| 3266 | `execute.test.ts` — "Waiting for Job controller…" log | 65 % |
| 3183 | `shared-doc-overlay.test.ts` — never overwrites a carried doc | 64 % |
| 2561 | `shared-doc-overlay.test.ts` — same, delivering from the Secret | 51 % |
| 2273 | `shared-doc-overlay.test.ts` — leaves the run workspace clean | 45 % |

All six passed; a seventh in the same file timed out at 6822 ms, overrunning by
1.8 s rather than hanging. That failure ejected `paperclip#3468` from the merge
queue at 2026-11-07T14:52:29Z — a `merge_group` failure is not a re-run, it
removes the PR and costs a human re-enqueue. The PR under test changed no file
under this tree, and the same job passed on both its own head (`e2068c37`) and
the identical base (`60af688d`) via another batch.

The 65 % is **structural, not contention**: the three `execute.test.ts` cases
reproduce at 3260-3262 ms on an idle machine, within ~2 % of their CI figures,
because they are driven by a fixed poll interval. Runner load is added on top
of a permanent 65 % floor rather than being the whole of it, so the exposure
sits on every run.

## Why suite-wide, and why 30 s

Six tests across two files share the exposure, so a per-test override on the
one that happened to lose is how this returns wearing a different test's name.

30 s matches the sibling `claude_k8s` adapter, which hit the same failure and
fixed it under BLO-48145 — same `arc-paperclip-light` pool, same
`npm ci` + `tsc` + `vitest` shape. One number across both adapters is one thing
to reason about. It puts the slowest known test at ~11 %.

No assertion changed, and a genuine hang still fails: the job's
`timeout-minutes: 17` (BLO-35615) remains the real hang detector.

## `hookTimeout` was measured and deliberately left unset

`shared-doc-overlay.test.ts`'s `beforeEach` does five real `git` spawns, so it
looked like the same shape. Probed by tightening `--hookTimeout` against that
file: the hook sits between 1000 ms (1 failure) and 1500 ms (clean) — 10-15 %
of vitest's 10 s default, against the test half's 65 %. Not an exposure today,
so it is not widened here.

If it ever becomes one it must be fixed **in this file**: a root-level CLI
`--hookTimeout` is inert under Vitest 4 `projects` (BLO-37184).

## Verification

Ran what the `Vendored opencode_k8s adapter` job runs: `npm ci --include=dev`,
`npx --no-install tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm test` 23 files / 760 tests passing
both before (81.8 s) and after (81.2 s).

Positive and negative control that the budget actually binds — a config change
that silently fails to apply is the fail-open shape that matters here. A
temporary 7 s probe test passes under the new config; forced back with
`--testTimeout=5000` the same probe reports `Test timed out in 5000ms.` and
fails. The probe was deleted; `src/vitest-config.test.ts` now carries that
guarantee permanently instead of as a one-off local probe.

## What this does not fix

It stops a latency problem being charged to the merge queue; it does not make
the six slow tests fast. If their runtime keeps climbing, the structural
3.26 s poll-interval wait in `execute.test.ts` is the thing to attack.
